nodes.label: Drive
nodes.note: What is delivered: device parameters, or an administered amount and route [199,24].

nodes.label: Effective stimulus
nodes.note: What acted on the tissue: field at the neuron, pressure at the transducing cell, concentration at the receptor, or a co-stimulated peripheral input [24,199].

nodes.label: Coupling
nodes.note: The physical or chemical event by which the drive first changes tissue [199].

nodes.label: Cellular
nodes.note: What a neuron or glial cell does in response [149].

nodes.label: Subcellular / molecular
nodes.note: Signalling that follows the cellular response and often outlasts the stimulus [149].

nodes.label: Circuit
nodes.note: How populations of connected cells change; wiring alone does not fix circuit function [5].

nodes.label: System
nodes.note: How a whole body system changes, such as arousal, autonomic or immune control [149].

nodes.label: Outcome
nodes.note: What is measured in the organism [199,24].

edges.label: is specified as
edges.note: Device parameters, or administered dose and route [9,24].

edges.label: is usually inferred, not measured
edges.note: Studies report the first and infer the second [24,199].

edges.label: changes what the cell does
edges.note: For ultrasound this arrow has rival paths, neuronal and astrocytic [69].

edges.label: biophysics to molecules
edges.note: Weakest join 1: the transducing cell and molecule are often unknown, and the drug side has the same gap between target and downstream step [69,168]. The Atlas's reading across the corpus, not a claim of any one source [24,69,199].

edges.label: changes populations in
edges.note: Needs its own measurement or model; wiring does not determine it [5,8].

edges.label: changes the state of
edges.note: Circuit-level theories carry much of the weight here [128,138].

edges.label: animal mechanism to human outcome
edges.note: Weakest join 2: in 43% of 44 Phase II programmes it was unclear whether the mechanism had been tested in people, and chronic-antidepressant accounts place middle-level frameworks between receptor occupancy and symptom change [24,187].

edges.label: afferent feedback: a reflex loop is a cycle, not a line
edges.note: Central integration sets how strongly the efferent limb fires [149].
